children: Lightspeed Venture Partners has raised more than $750 million so far for a new fund and related vehicle which would acquire existing businesses and upgrade them using artificial intelligence.

The venture firm, now headquartered in Menlo Park with plans to move to San Francisco, has already exceeded its initial target of $750 million for its AI Renaissance Fund and the related co-investment vehicle, Partner Isaac Kim told the New Mexico State Investment Council, the state's sovereign-wealth fund, at a public meeting on Tuesday.

In response to a question from a council member, Kim said his fundraising goal for AI Renaissance "was always a little bit higher" than the $750 million. He added that the fund would invest in between eight and 10 businesses, assuming a $1 billion raise for the main fund.

Richard Pugmire, a partner at investment adviser Marsh, which works with the New Mexico council, said at the meeting that the AI Renaissance Fund would do two types of deals. First, rollups, in which the fund would acquire multiple businesses and combine them into one company, the strategy focusing on industries like financial services, healthcare and engineering services, among others. The second is a "buy-and-build" strategy that will also target business services companies, according to a person familiar with the approach.

Lightspeed believes AI will reach the broader economy in two different ways, according to materials for the AI Renaissance Fund: through the creation of new, AI-native businesses, and the transformation of existing businesses using the technology. The AI Renaissance Fund will address that second path.

At the end of last year, Lightspeed announced it had raised more than $9 billion across six funds, the largest haul in its 25-year history. The firm's portfolio includes AI lab Anthropic, travel and expense management platform Navan and the social-media company Snap.

The firm has asserted its belief in the AI Renaissance strategy before: It participated in holding company Beacon Software's $225 million Series C, which closed earlier this year. Beacon acquires existing software companies, imbues them with an AI operating system and rolls them into a portfolio to hold indefinitely.
Kim will helm the investment team of the AI Renaissance Fund. He joined Lightspeed from Elliott Investment Management in 2024 to lead the firm's growth private-equity strategy.

At its meeting Tuesday, the New Mexico council approved a commitment of up to $100 million to the fund and another of up to $20 million for the related co-investment vehicle. Co-investment allows limited partners like the council to invest directly in venture-backed companies alongside venture firms. Lightspeed isn't charging fees or a portion of the vehicle's investment gains — known in venture as carry — on the co-investment vehicle, according to materials made public by the council.
The Illinois Municipal Retirement Fund, a public pension system, approved a commitment of up to $35 million to the AI Renaissance Fund in August, it said at the time.
